name: Philetus
overview: Philetus is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament, specifically noted for the destructive nature of his teachings, which are described as spreading like gangrene. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes. His influence is marked by the harmful impact of his speech within the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name Philetus appears once in Scripture without an explicit meaning provided. It is simply recognized as a proper name without additional linguistic or theological significance noted in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Philetus beyond what is indicated by his unique attribute. There are no known familial or relational connections detailed in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Philetus is significant in the biblical narrative as a cautionary example of false teaching that damages the church from within. His teachings, likened to gangrene, highlight the danger of corrupt doctrine spreading unchecked among believers. This serves as a warning to maintain sound doctrine and vigilance against those who would distort the gospel message.
